title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 94
paragraphs: After this our history proceeds to inquire about Cyrus, who he was that destroyed the empire of Croesus, and about the Persians, in what manner they obtained the lead of Asia. Following, then, the report of certain of the Persians—I mean those who do not desire to glorify the history of Cyrus but to speak what is in fact true—according to their report, I say, I shall write; though I could also set forth the other forms of the story in three different ways.

The Assyrians ruled Upper Asia for five hundred and twenty years, and from them the Medes were the first to revolt. These, having fought for their freedom against the Assyrians, proved themselves brave men, and so they pushed off the yoke of slavery from themselves and were set free. After them the other nations also did the same as the Medes; and when all on the continent were thus independent, they returned again to despotic rule as follows.
